title: Myanmar Hip-Hop Open Data Archive
description: Knowledge-graph style schema. All facts must carry at least one source ID and a confidence level.

fields.name: string
fields.city: string|null (origin or base; use base for diaspora acts)
fields.base: string|null (current base, e.g. 'Munich, Germany' for diaspora acts)
fields.realName: string|null (only when published by a cited source)
fields.genre: string[] (e.g. trap, drill, boom-bap, jersey club; only when sourced, never from a single platform genre field)

fields.name: string
fields.kind: crew | association | collective | label | studio | media

fields.title: string
fields.artistId: string (or artistIdA/artistIdB for a duo/collab billing)
fields.year: int|null (null when only a range or a re-release date is known)
fields.yearNote: string|null (explains a null or uncertain year)
fields.type: album | EP | single | mixtape | compilation | live | collection
encyclopedia | article | interview | podcast | video | database | magazine | journal | advocacy | music | website | archive | aggregator
fields.title: string
fields.author: string|absent
fields.archivedUrl: string|null (use when the live URL is dead)
fields.quality: primary | high | medium-high | medium | low | secondary | unverified

fields.label: string
fields.artistNames: string[] (named in the sources but not yet promoted to Artist records)
fields.confidence: string (free text; may qualify per claim)

fields.path: string (served by the consuming app, e.g. /media/...)

fields.type: diss track | crew exit | legal/censorship | legal/political | legal/other | credit dispute
fields.parties: artist or crew id[] (only where an entity record exists)
fields.partyNames: string[] (named in the sources but without an entity record)
fields.targetDescription: string|null (prose, NOT an id - the target is often the state or an unnamed person)
fields.period: string (free text: year, range, or 'documented 2016, ongoing')
fields.claim: string (what is alleged or what happened, always attributed)
fields.corroboration: string (must name whether the support is single-source)

fields.type: member_of | released | performed_at | pioneer_of | associated_with | mentioned_in | documented_in | signed_to | founded | featured_on | dissed | produced_for | part_of

rules: Every claim must reference at least one source ID.
No copyrighted text is stored - only factual metadata (names, dates, places).
Image records hold credits and source links only; binaries are not redistributed by this repository.
Image.alt and Image.credit are defaults. A Period may override both, because one image file is captioned differently in different periods.
Period.artistNames holds acts that the cited sources name but that have no Artist record yet. They are deliberately not promoted until an act-level source supports one.

A Dispute is a CLAIM by at least one party, often disputed by the other. Never state an allegation as established fact: record who claimed it, what the claim is, and whether it is corroborated. `corroboration` must say 'single-source' where that is the case.

Dispute.status distinguishes settled (documented) from disputed (two incompatible accounts) from unresolved (evidence is thin or the primary source is dead) from structurally unresolved (the mechanism itself is the finding, e.g. an absent legal category).

Do not create a causal link between two events merely because sources place them adjacently. The Y-Zet concert death of 2017 and the 'Shwee Die' diss of 2011 are six years apart and the fatal fight began with accidental contact while dancing.

In this scene 'beef' is usually a genre label or a song title, not a documented grievance. Multi-artist posse cuts titled with the word 'beef' are not feuds. Only code a Dispute where a claim, a target and some evidence exist.
Where a dispute targets a living person who is deliberately unnamed in the work itself, keep them unnamed. A veiled diss stays veiled.
Conflicts are flagged as CONFLICTED and resolved by human review, never by AI.
Burmese script names are preserved in the aliases field.

identityStatus is mandatory whenever realName is null. Use 'pseudonym' or 'anonymised' for post-coup acts whose legal identity is deliberately withheld. Never infer a real name from a pseudonym, a producer credit, or a shared surname.
Never attribute a real name to someone at risk. A stage name published in press stays a stage name.
Release.year may be null when only a re-release date or an uncertain range is known; explain it in yearNote. Do not silently convert a platform date into a release year.
Suspected re-releases are flagged in Release.note rather than presented as a second, earlier release.
Conflicting counts or dates are preserved with both values and their sources. Do not harmonise a disagreement the sources have not resolved.
Genre is recorded only when a cited source states it. A single streaming platform's genre field is metadata, not a stylistic claim; it is not sufficient on its own.

Third-party AI music-analytics aggregators (musicmetricsvault, sounddrain, viberate) publish fabricated prose and invented statistics. Never cite them. Platform metadata may be cited only from the platform itself.
When a source is offline, cite it via archivedUrl (web.archive.org). A dead URL is not a reason to drop a well-evidenced fact.
Platform artist pages are ambiguous for generic names. Record the platform's numeric artist id on the Source so a future checker can disambiguate collisions.
